html:
The discovery of the Higgs boson, announced on 4 July 2012 at CERN, the European physics laboratory near Geneva. Two huge detectors at the Large Hadron Collider both found a new particle with the mass the theory expected.

The particle had been predicted in 1964 by Peter Higgs, François Englert and others. Their idea was a field filling all of space; particles that interact with it gain mass. The Higgs boson is a ripple in that field, and it was the last missing piece of the Standard Model of particle physics.

Finding it took nearly 50 years and a machine that smashes protons together in a 27 km ring under the French Swiss border, built and run by thousands of scientists from many countries. Higgs and Englert shared the Nobel Prize in 2013. CERN, founded in 1954 to rebuild European science after the war, also gave the world the World Wide Web.
